clue.text: Books time off, shortly, somewhere in Canada

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first books of the Bible

indicators.note: said shortly, the word for off loses its final letter

parts.note: off in the sense of away, absent

explanation.surface: Someone takes a quick break from their reading somewhere in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Canada is one place in that country, so a vague locator fits.

clue.text: To English newspaper, he's a despicable sort

parts.note: a rag is a slang term for a low-grade newspaper

explanation.surface: A man is denounced as contemptible in a letter to an English paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A toerag is British slang for a contemptible, worthless person; it means a scoundrel.

clue.text: Works of art made from lace a priest spread out

indicators.note: spreading things out disturbs their order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Church artworks are said to be made from lace a priest laid out.
explanation.definitionFit: An altarpiece is a painting or carving placed behind a church altar, a kind of artwork.

clue.text: In several countries, fix right time to sow species of plant

indicators.note: sowing scatters seed, so the letters of the word time are scattered into a new order

parts.note: Asia is a continent made up of several countries

indicators.note: to fix something in a place is to set it inside, so these letters go into the continent

explanation.surface: Gardeners abroad try to settle on the right moment for planting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to sow' scatters the letters of the word time into EMI; 'fix' sets the result, with R, inside the continent. 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is a genus of aromatic plants including wormwood and mugwort, so it names a plant type.

clue.text: Lover of luxury's place, round ultimately trendy pub

indicators.note: the word for place is set round the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a site is a place or location

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the next word

parts.note: a bar is a pub or drinking place

explanation.surface: A pleasure-seeker's favourite spot is a fashionable pub nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive on luxury is a link meaning is, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sybarite is someone devoted to luxury and sensual pleasure, after the ancient Greek city of Sybaris.

clue.text: More flexible caterer one's forgotten

indicators.note: something forgotten is left out, so the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a supplier is one who caters or provides goods
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A catering firm seems more adaptable once one item slips its mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Supple means bendy or pliant, so the comparative form means bending more easily.

clue.text: Butler turned on member of nobility

indicators.note: turned means the name is read backwards

parts.note: Rab Butler was a prominent British Conservative politician of the mid-twentieth century
taken as written

explanation.surface: A butler rounds on an aristocrat he serves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes RAB into BAR. The capital B on Butler disguises the politician as a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A baron is a rank in the peerage, so he is one member of the nobility.

clue.text: Drive hard down motorway, after a right turn

indicators.note: after places the motorway letter behind the other two
a turn swings these letters round, so they are read backwards

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A motorist speeds down a motorway after turning right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes AR into RA, and 'after' puts M behind it; 'down' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To ram something is to force or drive it in hard, as with a ram.

clue.text: One boarding streetcar is head of university's Italian course

indicators.note: someone boarding a vehicle gets inside it, so the letter goes inside the word

parts.note: a tram is a streetcar running on rails in the street
I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A university chief hops on a tram for an Italian lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boarding' puts I inside TRAM. The surface suggests a language course; it is a dessert course.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is a coffee-flavoured Italian dessert, eaten as one course of a meal.

clue.text: Train spotters in lay-by next to highway

indicators.note: to train is to direct or shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Trainspotters gather in a lay-by beside the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A rest stop is a roadside parking area where drivers pull off the highway to take a break.

clue.text: Comment on model

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
a mark is a model or version, as in Mark II

explanation.surface: Someone passes comment on a fashion model.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark is a spoken observation or comment.

clue.text: Tramp imbibing port as medicinal drink?

indicators.note: imbibing means drinking in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant
Ayr is a port on the west coast of Scotland

explanation.surface: A vagrant drinks port as if it were medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits bay rum is really a hair lotion, though its name suggests a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay rum is an aromatic lotion distilled with rum and bay leaves, so the question mark licenses calling it a medicinal drink.

clue.text: Sole mortgage — amount of money being discussed?

indicators.note: being discussed means spoken about, so the pieces are heard rather than read

parts.note: a mortgage is a loan for a house; a sum is an amount of money

explanation.surface: A lone house buyer thinks over a mortgage figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being discussed' says LOAN SUM is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole can mean alone and solitary, which is the feeling of being lonely and isolated.

clue.text: Arch-priest's organised examination

indicators.note: organising things arranges them anew, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A senior cleric arranges an inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip-search is a search of a person's naked body, a kind of examination by police or guards.

clue.text: Teacher in state of tension about the endless traffic

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for tension encloses the other letters

parts.note: stress is a state of mental or physical tension

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: truck means dealings or traffic, as in having no truck with someone

explanation.surface: A stressed teacher is worried by the never-ending traffic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts the trimmed word inside, after the first letter of the word for tension; 'the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An instructress is a woman who teaches or instructs, the feminine form of instructor.

clue.text: I cannot succeed alone

parts.note: succeed is read as inheriting a title or estate; one who shares an inheritance cannot inherit alone

explanation.definitionFit: A coheritor is a joint heir, someone who inherits together with others rather than solely.

clue.text: Plant, one vicar cultivated

indicators.note: cultivating soil turns it over, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A clergyman grows a flower in the vicarage garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Veronica, or speedwell, is a genus of flowering plants, so it is one kind of plant.

clue.text: French sea songs, in style on trading boat

parts.note: mer is the French word for sea
chants are songs, especially sung in unison
hip means fashionable or in style

explanation.surface: Sailors sing sea shanties in fine style aboard a cargo vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant ship is a vessel carrying cargo for trade rather than for war.

clue.text: Artist upset, initially ordered to run with it

indicators.note: in a down answer, upset turns the letters upside down, reading them from the bottom
initially points to the first letter of the next word

parts.note: to lope is to run with a long easy stride
taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter, shaken, is told to make a run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns O + LOPE + IT so it reads from the bottom: OLOPEIT becomes the answer. 'to' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Giovanni Battista Tiepolo was an eighteenth-century Venetian painter famous for ceiling frescoes.

clue.text: Maybe 6's head is chopped off-in French town

indicators.note: chopped off means the word for head is cut away from the front

parts.note: 6 down is a baron, which is an example of a nobleman
nob is slang for the head

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is beheaded in a provincial French town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped off' removes NOB from NOBLEMAN'S. 'Maybe' says a baron is only one kind of nobleman.
explanation.definitionFit: Le Mans is a town in north-western France, famous for its 24-hour motor race.

clue.text: Not all one's own work

parts.note: reads like a confession of plagiarism, but describes an arrangement where two people divide one post between them

explanation.definitionFit: A job-share is an arrangement in which two part-timers split one full-time position.

clue.text: Indian disposes of horse quickly

parts.note: the Apache are a Native American people
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: A Native American rider quickly gets rid of his horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Apace is an adverb meaning swiftly or at a fast rate.

clue.text: Interior of Greek edifice was humming

indicators.note: the interior of a phrase is the run of letters inside it, here spanning both words

explanation.surface: Inside an ancient Greek building, something smelled or buzzed.
explanation.definitionFit: Humming is slang for smelling bad, and reeked means gave off a strong unpleasant smell.

clue.text: Square meal in Italy? Adult tucks in

parts.note: pizza is a typical Italian meal

explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks in' puts A inside PIZZA. 'Square meal' reads as one phrase, but Square is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A piazza is an open public square in an Italian town.

parts.words: Character comes last in quiz, we've heard

parts.note: a rash is an outbreak of spots on the skin

indicators.note: back means the word is read in reverse

parts.note: he is a fellow, a man
